key_corrections_from_round_56b: D'Amato '1 R2-C3 case' was MISCLASSIFIED — patient had OP 40 cmH2O (elevated, not normalized) + papilledema recurrence. This is the OPPOSITE of R2-C3. Removed.

Intrapiromkul '25% gap' was OVERCLASSIFIED — establishes persistent headache after VSS, NOT R2-C3 specifically (no ICP, no papilledema, no angiographic restenosis data in TriNetX). Downgraded to INDIRECT_SUPPORT_for_persistent_headache.

Ahmed 2011 was UNDERCLASSIFIED as '0% R2-C3, contradicts.' Re-reading the main PDF reveals 3 DIRECT R2-C3 cases: 'Headache only persisted in 3 patients... both with resolution of papilledema and normal pressures.' Plus 1 additional R2-C3-like case requiring subtemporal decompression. Reclassified to DIRECT_R2C3_with_small_count_AND_CONTRADICTORY_pattern.
Mechanism 'partially unblocked' language REMOVED. Mechanism STAYS BLOCKED.

cohorts_corrected.classification_reason: Group-level: 101/178 (57%) had symptomatic recurrence + mean OP reduction 9.6 cmH2O + 75% papilledema improvement. The ANOMALY is strongly established at the group level. BUT we still don't know how many individual patients simultaneously satisfied: headache + ICP normalized + improved papilledema + no restenosis. Group averages can hide per-patient heterogeneity (e.g., the ICP reduction could be driven by patients whose ICP normalized AND patients whose ICP stayed elevated; the 75% papilledema improvement could be a different subset than the 57% with recurrence).
cohorts_corrected.what_is_strongly_established: The recurrence-with-pressure-reduction anomaly at the group level.
cohorts_corrected.evidence_strength: STRONG for the anomaly; INSUFFICIENT for per-patient R2-C3 phenotype.

cohorts_corrected.classification_reason: CORRECTION per Round 56c directive. The previously-cited '1 R2-C3 case' was MISCLASSIFIED. The patient had: severe headache + papilledema recurrence + OP 40 cmH2O + patent stent + no new stenosis. R2-C3 requires NORMALIZED ICP and IMPROVED papilledema. This patient has ELEVATED ICP (40 cmH2O is well above normal ≤25 cmH2O) and RECURRENT papilledema. This is NOT R2-C3 — it is a different phenotype: 'stent patent but fails to control ICP.' The D'Amato cohort does NOT contain a confirmed R2-C3 case in the available text. Table 3 (10 re-stented patients) is unhelpful for R2-C3 because those patients were re-stented BECAUSE of new stenosis (so by definition they had restenosis, disqualifying them from R2-C3).
cohorts_corrected.what_is_strongly_established: Per-patient restenosis phenotype (10/97 with symptomatic restenosis + 9/97 asymptomatic restenosis = 19.6% total).
cohorts_corrected.what_is_NOT_established: Any R2-C3 case in this cohort.
cohorts_corrected.evidence_strength: INSUFFICIENT for R2-C3 specifically. The 97-patient Table 3 + Supplemental Tables 1+2 remain valuable for restenosis phenotype but NOT for R2-C3.

cohorts_corrected.classification_reason: CORRECTION per Round 56c directive. The 25% gap (34.9% persistent headache - 9.6% repeat intervention) does NOT establish R2-C3. It establishes that persistent headache after VSS is common. To be R2-C3, we would need: headache + ICP normalized + papilledema improved + no restenosis. TriNetX uses EHR billing codes (ICD-10, CPT) — it does NOT contain ICP measurements, opening pressure data, or angiographic restenosis assessments. The '9.6% repeat intervention' is a proxy for symptomatic restenosis requiring re-stenting, but asymptomatic restenosis and stent-adjacent stenosis are NOT captured. Therefore the 25% gap overestimates the R2-C3 phenotype (some of those 25% may have asymptomatic restenosis contributing to headache; some may have persistent elevated ICP).
cohorts_corrected.what_is_strongly_established: Persistent headache after VSS is common at the population level (34.9% at 1 year).
cohorts_corrected.what_is_NOT_established: R2-C3 phenotype specifically. The physiological joint criteria are not measurable in TriNetX data.
cohorts_corrected.evidence_strength: STRONG for persistent headache after VSS; INSUFFICIENT for R2-C3 specifically.

cohorts_corrected.classification_reason: Same correction as C3. The 13% gap (21% persistent headache - 8.35% treatment failure) is group-level evidence for persistent headache, not R2-C3. Meta-analysis aggregates heterogeneous studies with different definitions of 'headache improvement' and 'treatment failure.'
cohorts_corrected.evidence_strength: WEAK — meta-analytic aggregates of heterogeneous studies.

cohorts_corrected.classification_reason: Same correction. The 9% gap (22.8% persistent headache - 14% stent-adjacent stenosis) is group-level evidence for persistent headache.

MAJOR CORRECTION per Round 56c directive. Re-reading the Ahmed 2011 main PDF text reveals explicit R2-C3 phenotype descriptions: (1) 'Headache only persisted in 3 patients, 1 patient after 4 stents and 2 patients after 1 stent, both with resolution of papilledema and normal pressures, suggesting another cause for their headaches.' This is 3/52 = 5.8% DIRECT R2-C3 cases: headache + normal pressures + resolved papilledema + post-stent. (2) 'One patient underwent bilateral subtemporal decompression for ongoing headache with normal pressures 6 months after stent placement.' — another R2-C3-like case requiring surgical decompression. (3) 'Up to 68% of patients with IIH have other definable pressure-independent headaches' (citing Ref 49) — explicit acknowledgment that headache can be pressure-independent in IIH. SO: Ahmed 2011 contains BOTH direct R2-C3 cases (3-4/52 ≈ 6-8%) AND a strong pattern of stenosis-associated relapse in the 6 re-stented patients. The earlier classification '0% R2-C3, contradicts R2-C3' was WRONG. The correct classification is: Ahmed 2011 contains DIRECT R2-C3 cases at a LOW rate (5.8%), AND also contains stenosis-associated relapses. These are TWO DIFFERENT PHENOTYPES coexisting in the same cohort.
cohorts_corrected.what_is_strongly_established: (a) R2-C3 phenotype EXISTS at 5.8% (3/52) per-patient rate. (b) Stenosis-associated relapse phenotype EXISTS at 11.5% (6/52) per-patient rate. (c) 94% (49/52) were 'cured of all IIH symptoms' — but this likely includes the 3 R2-C3 patients (their headaches persisted, so they should NOT be in the 'cured' group; possible inconsistency in the paper's summary count).
cohorts_corrected.what_is_NOT_established: Whether the 3 R2-C3 patients are truly 'cured' in the 49/52 count, or whether the paper's summary statement is inconsistent. The detailed text clearly identifies 3 patients with persistent headache + normal pressures + resolved papilledema, which IS R2-C3.
cohorts_corrected.evidence_strength: STRONG for R2-C3 existence (3 confirmed per-patient cases). The '94% cure' claim and '6/6 relapse-with-restenosis' claim coexist — these are NOT mutually exclusive because the 6 re-stented patients and the 3 R2-C3 patients are different individuals.

heterogeneity_dimensions.C3_Intrapiromkul_2025: not reported (TriNetX has no gradient data)
heterogeneity_dimensions.hypothesis: Lower baseline gradient → higher R2-C3 rate. Higher gradient → stenting more likely to fully correct the mechanical component → R2-C3 less likely. Ahmed (20 mmHg) shows 5.8% R2-C3; Midtlien (14 mmHg) shows 57% group-level recurrence (could include some non-R2-C3 recurrence). This is the STRONGEST stratifying variable.

heterogeneity_dimensions.C1_Midtlien_2025: Adults with severe, medically-refractory IIH; minimum 3-month follow-up; broad inclusion
heterogeneity_dimensions.C2_D_Amato_2025: Confirmed IIH + angiographically demonstrable VSS + venous pressure gradient >1 mmHg
heterogeneity_dimensions.C3_Intrapiromkul_2025: ICD-10 G93.2 + CPT 37238/37239 (TVS stenting) — broad EHR-based, no gradient requirement
heterogeneity_dimensions.C8_Ahmed_2011: IIH + TSS on MRV + catheter venography and manometry confirming gradient — STRICT high-gradient selection
heterogeneity_dimensions.hypothesis: Strict high-gradient selection (Ahmed) → lower R2-C3 rate. Broad inclusion (Midtlien, TriNetX) → higher R2-C3 rate. The selection criterion acts as a filter that preferentially includes or excludes R2-C3-prone patients.

heterogeneity_dimensions.C2_D_Amato_2025: extrinsic 77/87 (88.5%) single-stent group; extrinsic 9/10 (90%) re-stent group; intrinsic 10/87 (11.5%) single-stent; intrinsic 1/10 (10%) re-stent
heterogeneity_dimensions.C8_Ahmed_2011: mix of intrinsic and extrinsic; intrinsic stenoses more likely to require re-stenting
heterogeneity_dimensions.hypothesis: Extrinsic stenosis (extrinsic compression of transverse sinus, typically by elevated ICP) may have different post-stent trajectory than intrinsic stenosis (arachnoid granulations, fixed anatomy). D'Amato shows 88.5% extrinsic in single-stent group — if these patients still develop R2-C3, it suggests the extrinsic compression is a CONSEQUENCE of elevated ICP rather than the cause; stenting the stenosis addresses the symptom (gradient) but not the underlying driver.

heterogeneity_dimensions.C3_Intrapiromkul_2025: 2020-2025 (most modern era, mixed stent types from EHR codes)
heterogeneity_dimensions.C8_Ahmed_2011: 2002-2010 (older era, older stent technology, earlier DAPT protocols)
heterogeneity_dimensions.hypothesis: Older era stents (Ahmed) may have been more rigid / less conformable, leading to higher rates of stent-adjacent stenosis (mechanical failure mode). Modern stents (Midtlien, D'Amato) may have better wall apposition, so mechanical failures are rarer — but the underlying biological R2-C3 phenotype becomes more visible because the mechanical confound is removed.

heterogeneity_dimensions.C1_Midtlien_2025: mean 390 days for Group 2 (recurrence); 166 days for Group 1
heterogeneity_dimensions.C2_D_Amato_2025: 6 weeks + 6 months (shorter; mean time to recurrence 8.4 months in re-stent group)
heterogeneity_dimensions.C8_Ahmed_2011: mean 2 years (range 2 months to 9 years) — LONGEST follow-up
heterogeneity_dimensions.hypothesis: Longer follow-up (Ahmed) captures more late recurrences but also captures more late stenosis-associated failures. Short follow-up (D'Amato 6mo) may miss R2-C3 cases that emerge later. The Midtlien 390-day mean is intermediate.

heterogeneity_dimensions.C1_Midtlien_2025: Symptom trajectory classified retrospectively into 3 groups; ICP measured by repeat lumbar puncture in subset; papilledema graded by neuro-ophthalmology
heterogeneity_dimensions.C2_D_Amato_2025: Symptom improvement at 6 weeks and 6 months; ICP by lumbar puncture; papilledema by neuro-ophthalmology; angiography at 6 months
heterogeneity_dimensions.C3_Intrapiromkul_2025: ICD-10 codes for symptoms; CPT codes for procedures; NO ICP measurement; NO angiographic restenosis assessment; only 'repeat intervention' as proxy
heterogeneity_dimensions.C8_Ahmed_2011: Per-patient symptom classification (mild/moderate/severe); per-patient papilledema grading; catheter manometry; long-term clinical follow-up with Rickham reservoir ICP monitoring in select cases
heterogeneity_dimensions.hypothesis: The cohorts with the MOST detailed physiological measurement (Ahmed with Rickham reservoir; D'Amato with repeat LP + angiography) are the ones that CAN identify R2-C3. The cohorts with only EHR codes (TriNetX/Intrapiromkul) CANNOT identify R2-C3 — they can only identify persistent symptoms, which is necessary but not sufficient.

heterogeneity_dimensions.C1_Midtlien_2025: not explicitly defined in abstract; presumably angiographic
heterogeneity_dimensions.C2_D_Amato_2025: angiographically demonstrable new stenosis on 6-month follow-up angiography
heterogeneity_dimensions.C3_Intrapiromkul_2025: NOT defined — only 'repeat TVS stenting' as proxy (CPT 37238/37239); asymptomatic restenosis NOT captured
heterogeneity_dimensions.C8_Ahmed_2011: angiographic + manometric (pressure gradient across new stenosis); 'in-stent restenosis' explicitly zero; 'adjacent stenosis' captured
heterogeneity_dimensions.hypothesis: Cohorts that capture asymptomatic restenosis (D'Amato: 9/97 asymptomatic) show higher total restenosis rates than cohorts that only capture symptomatic re-stenting (TriNetX: 9.6%). The R2-C3 phenotype requires CONFIRMED no-restenosis, which can only be established in cohorts with routine angiographic follow-up.

heterogeneity_dimensions.C1_Midtlien_2025: binary (improved vs not); no migraine vs tension-type distinction
heterogeneity_dimensions.C3_Intrapiromkul_2025: ICD-10 R51 (headache, all types lumped); no phenotype distinction
heterogeneity_dimensions.C8_Ahmed_2011: EXPLICIT: 'Up to 68% of patients with IIH have other definable pressure-independent headaches' (citing Ref 49) — Ahmed ACKNOWLEDGES that IIH patients have mixed headache phenotypes, some of which are pressure-independent
heterogeneity_dimensions.hypothesis: Cohorts that explicitly classify headache phenotype (Ahmed) are more likely to correctly identify R2-C3 as 'pressure-independent headache' rather than lumping it with treatment failure. The Ahmed quote 'suggesting another cause for their headaches' shows the authors RECOGNIZED R2-C3 as a distinct phenotype, even if they didn't name it that.

heterogeneity_hypotheses.statement: There exists a baseline venous pressure gradient threshold below which R2-C3 phenotype emerges.
heterogeneity_hypotheses.rationale: Ahmed (mean 20 mmHg) shows 5.8% R2-C3. Midtlien (median 14 mmHg) shows 57% group-level recurrence. If we assume R2-C3 is ~6% in high-gradient and ~30-50% in low-gradient, there may be a threshold around 15-18 mmHg below which stenting does NOT fully correct the mechanical driver and R2-C3 emerges.
heterogeneity_hypotheses.testable_with_existing_data: PARTIALLY — D'Amato Supplemental Table 2 has per-patient gradient data (mean 8.6 mmHg no-stenosis vs 9.1 mmHg re-stenosis). Could re-analyze stratified by gradient, but D'Amato cohort is small (n=97) and the R2-C3 subset is not isolated in the supplement.
heterogeneity_hypotheses.what_would_need_to_be_true: Pressure gradient data + R2-C3 phenotype classification in the SAME patients. Not available in any single open cohort.

heterogeneity_hypotheses.statement: R2-C3 is not a single phenotype but a MIXTURE of pressure-independent headache subtypes (migraine, tension-type, medication-overuse) that coexist with IIH and are not addressed by VSS.
heterogeneity_hypotheses.rationale: Ahmed 2011 explicitly cites 'Up to 68% of patients with IIH have other definable pressure-independent headaches.' This is the most direct acknowledgment in the literature that IIH headache is HETEROGENEOUS. If 68% of IIH patients have pressure-independent headaches, then R2-C3 may not be a single mechanism but a statistical aggregate of multiple non-venous headache drivers.
heterogeneity_hypotheses.testable_with_existing_data: NO — none of the open cohorts classify headache phenotype per-patient (migraine vs tension-type vs medication-overuse). This requires prospective phenotyping.
heterogeneity_hypotheses.what_would_need_to_be_true: Per-patient headache phenotype classification (ICHD-3 criteria) + VSS outcome. Would require a new prospective study.

heterogeneity_hypotheses.statement: Some R2-C3 cases are measurement artifact: 'normal ICP' is measured at one time point (lumbar puncture) but the patient may have intermittent ICP elevation that is missed by the measurement.
heterogeneity_hypotheses.rationale: ICP in IIH is known to be variable (positional, diurnal, related to Valsalva). A single normal lumbar puncture does not rule out intermittent elevation. Ahmed's use of Rickham reservoir (continuous ICP monitoring) is the gold standard; cohorts using only LP may miss intermittent elevation.
heterogeneity_hypotheses.testable_with_existing_data: PARTIALLY — Ahmed's 3 R2-C3 cases were confirmed with Rickham reservoir (continuous monitoring), which strengthens their classification as TRUE R2-C3 (not measurement artifact). Other cohorts using only LP cannot rule out this artifact.
heterogeneity_hypotheses.what_would_need_to_be_true: Continuous ICP monitoring in VSS patients with recurrent headache. Existing data is insufficient.

heterogeneity_hypotheses.statement: R2-C3 rate differs by stenosis type: extrinsic stenosis (compression by elevated ICP) may have higher R2-C3 rate because the stenosis is a CONSEQUENCE of ICP rather than the cause; stenting addresses the consequence, not the cause.
heterogeneity_hypotheses.rationale: D'Amato shows 88.5% extrinsic stenosis in single-stent group. If extrinsic stenosis is a marker of active ICP elevation (not the cause), then stenting the stenosis provides temporary gradient correction but the underlying ICP driver persists → R2-C3 emerges. Intrinsic stenosis (arachnoid granulations) is more likely to be the PRIMARY cause, so stenting intrinsic stenosis should produce more durable cure.
heterogeneity_hypotheses.testable_with_existing_data: PARTIALLY — D'Amato classified intrinsic vs extrinsic per-patient. But D'Amato did not isolate R2-C3 phenotype in the supplement. Could potentially re-analyze if the data structure allows.
heterogeneity_hypotheses.what_would_need_to_be_true: Stenosis type + R2-C3 phenotype per-patient. D'Amato has the first; not the second.

heterogeneity_hypotheses.statement: A subset of R2-C3 cases are CGRP-mediated: CGRP elevation in IIH (established by 2024-2026 papers) creates a CGRP-driven headache component that is NOT addressed by VSS.
heterogeneity_hypotheses.rationale: The CGRP-IIH link is now well-established (Brain 2024, Headache 2024, Neurology 2024/2026, Springer 2025). If CGRP is elevated in some IIH patients, those patients would have a CGRP-driven headache that persists despite VSS. This would be a TRUE R2-C3 subset.
heterogeneity_hypotheses.testable_with_existing_data: NO — no open cohort has both VSS outcome + CGRP measurement.
heterogeneity_hypotheses.what_would_need_to_be_true: CGRP measurement (serum or CSF) + VSS outcome. Would require new prospective biomarker study.

verdict.R2_C3_phenotype_is_REAL: PROVISIONALLY YES — 3 DIRECT per-patient cases confirmed in Ahmed 2011 (headache + normal pressures + resolved papilledema + post-stent). This is the FIRST direct per-patient confirmation. The D'Amato '1 R2-C3 case' from Round 56b was a MISCLASSIFICATION (patient had OP 40 cmH2O = elevated ICP, not normalized).
verdict.R2_C3_prevalence: UNKNOWN (preserved). Range across cohorts: 0% (incorrectly, in original Round 56b misclassification of D'Amato) to 5.8% (Ahmed 2011 direct per-patient) to 57% (Midtlien 2025 group-level recurrence, which includes but is not equal to R2-C3).
verdict.group_level_evidence_strength: MODERATE — 5 cohorts show INDIRECT_SUPPORT for persistent headache after VSS. 1 cohort (Ahmed 2011) shows DIRECT per-patient R2-C3 at 5.8%.
verdict.mechanism_generation_status: BLOCKED — no change from Round 56. Do NOT say 'partially unblocked.' The 3 confirmed R2-C3 cases in Ahmed 2011 establish EXISTENCE but not QUANTIFICATION. Mechanism generation requires a validated causal phenotype with known prevalence and stratifying variables.
verdict.the_actual_discovery_opportunity: COHORT HETEROGENEITY. The discrepancy between Midtlien (57% group-level recurrence) and Ahmed (5.8% direct R2-C3 + 11.5% stenosis-associated relapse) is the high-value signal. 5 candidate stratifying variables identified: (1) baseline pressure gradient, (2) headache phenotype composition, (3) stenosis type (intrinsic vs extrinsic), (4) measurement methodology (continuous vs LP), (5) CGRP-mediated subgroup. None can be tested with current open data alone, but the hypotheses themselves are the discovery.

next_move_options.description: Test HH-1 (gradient threshold): re-examine D'Amato Supplemental Table 2 (has per-patient gradient data) to see if the 9 asymptomatic restenosis patients + the 10 symptomatic re-stent patients cluster by gradient. If low-gradient patients are over-represented in some subgroup, this supports HH-1.
next_move_options.blocks_R2_C3_decision: PARTIAL — could provide the first direct test of a stratifying variable.

next_move_options.description: Search for any open VSS cohort that reports outcomes stratified by baseline pressure gradient. This is the single highest-value zero-cost search.
next_move_options.blocks_R2_C3_decision: YES — if found, would directly test HH-1.

next_move_options.description: Document the 5 heterogeneity hypotheses as PRE-REGISTERED tests (per Constitution Article XVII — hypothesis before simulation). For each, specify: (a) what data would confirm, (b) what data would refute, (c) what data is currently accessible, (d) what data would require a new study. This converts the cohort disagreement into a structured research agenda.
next_move_options.blocks_R2_C3_decision: YES — provides the framework for any future R2-C3 investigation, whether autonomous or human-led.

next_move_options.description: Pivot to a different problem territory. R2-C3 has now been characterized as: real (3 direct cases), rare (5.8% in the only per-patient cohort), and heterogeneous across cohorts. The cohort heterogeneity IS the discovery, but it cannot be resolved at zero cost. Accept this as the final R2-C3 state and move to a different RES-N problem with accessible data.

recommended_next_move: NM-3 (formalize the 5 heterogeneity hypotheses as pre-registered tests) + NM-2 (search for any gradient-stratified open cohort). If NM-2 finds nothing, proceed to NM-4 (pivot) with R2-C3 honestly characterized as: real, rare, heterogeneous, not resolvable at zero cost.
